D007-D015_h001.question:
I’ve been struggling for about the last seven months—maybe a bit longer. I wake up every day around 3 a.m., no matter what, and just lie there, staring at the ceiling. Falling back asleep feels impossible. I used to take pride in closing a tough case, but now? Nothing feels meaningful. Winning doesn’t matter. Losing doesn’t either. It’s like I’m watching my life through a thick window. Even simple things, like picking up coffee or signing documents, take forever—my body just drags.

Lately, it’s like the world is *talking* to me. Not directly, but in signs. A commercial on TV, a stranger’s cough in the courtroom—suddenly it feels coded, like they’re sending me messages only I understand. Last week, I saw my late father standing near the elevator in my office building. He didn’t speak. Just looked at me. I know he’s gone, but it was *real*—his coat, his hands. I’ve seen him a few times since.

My thoughts jump around sometimes. I’ll start talking about a client’s discharge petition and end up describing the wallpaper in my mother’s old apartment. My colleagues notice. I can tell they’re concerned.  

But it’s not constant. Some days the thoughts are quieter, but the heaviness in my chest never lifts. I can’t say whether the strange thoughts started before the sadness or after—everything just blurred together.
D007-D015_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D007-D015_h001.answer: D & C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h002.question:
I’ve not been myself for about seven months now—maybe longer. Some days, the sadness just drapes over me like a wet blanket. I don’t enjoy my garden like I used to, and I can’t even summon the energy to read, though I’ve always loved books. Falling asleep takes hours, even when I’m exhausted. My voice feels heavy, too—like words have to climb uphill before they come out.  

But it’s more than just sadness. My husband passed five years ago, God rest him, but sometimes I *see* him standing in the hallway, or at the foot of the bed, just watching. Other times, it’s strangers—people in old-fashioned coats, though they vanish when I turn on the light. And… I know it sounds foolish, but I’ve become convinced he was unfaithful near the end. I find myself searching his old drawers, looking for letters or receipts, certain there's proof I never found.  

I try to explain what I see, what I feel, but the thoughts get tangled—sometimes I can’t finish sentences, and people just stare. I don’t know if these things are real or if my mind is betraying me. They’ve been happening since the depression started… or maybe a bit before? I can’t recall exactly.
D007-D015_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D007-D015_h002.answer: D & C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h003.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about the last seven months, maybe a bit longer. The sadness is constant—it’s like a weight I can’t shake, no matter what I do. I used to find comfort in small things—reading, walking in the park, even my work with clients—but now nothing moves me. I don’t feel joy, not even when my niece laughs on the phone. Some mornings, I wake up at 3 a.m., wide awake, heart racing, just staring at the ceiling. I can’t go back to sleep, and by the time I have to get up, I feel like I’ve already lost the day.

Moving is hard now—not physically, but like my body resists. I used to be quick, efficient, but now I notice I’m slow, like I’m wading through water.  

And then there are the smells. I keep catching this sharp, burnt odor—like plastic on fire—but no one else does. It comes out of nowhere. Sometimes I think I’m meant to detect it—that maybe I’m being given a signal. I’ve started to wonder if I’m different somehow, specially chosen. There are moments I feel like I’m on the verge of understanding something huge, like I could unlock truths no one else sees.  

My thoughts jump around, I know. I’ll be talking about one thing and end up somewhere else without meaning to. It’s hard to explain.

    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h004.question:

I don’t enjoy auditions anymore—used to love them, now they’re just empty. Nothing feels real, not even the rare callbacks.  

But it’s not just sadness. Sometimes, I see figures in the corners of my apartment—like shadows with faces, watching me. They don’t speak, but I know they’re there. And I *know*, I really know, that I’m not just another struggling actor. There’s a reason I keep getting rejected—Hollywood isn’t ready for what I’m meant to do. I think I might be the key to something way bigger than films. Like, I’m destined to reveal truths no one else can see.  

I try to explain this, but my thoughts get tangled. I’ll start a sentence and lose the words halfway, like they melt. And the dreams—every night, I’m on stage, but the audience is made of mannequins that slowly turn into those shadow people. I wake up screaming.  

The voices haven’t come yet, but the visions… they’ve been with me just as long as the sadness. Or was it the other way around? I can’t remember when one started without the other.

    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h005.question:

Directing used to light me up, but now nothing does. I don’t feel joy when I finish a cut, not even when my son laughs on the phone. Everything feels… hollow. Talking takes effort—like my thoughts have to swim through mud. I pause too long when people ask simple questions. It’s embarrassing.

But it’s not just sadness. I keep seeing figures at the edge of the frame, like extras in a film that shouldn’t be there—standing in doorways, watching. They vanish when I turn. And lately, I’m certain the world’s already ended—just nobody told the living. It’s all a rerun. A *glitchtream*, I call it. That’s what I whispered to my assistant the other day. She didn’t understand. *Glitchtream*. It makes sense to me.

These visions, these thoughts—they’ve been with me nearly as long as the heaviness. But I can’t say which came first, or if one holds the other up like scaffolding. I just know the set feels empty even when it’s crowded.

    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h006.question:

I’ve lost about ten pounds without trying, just from not caring to eat. My husband notices how quiet I’ve gotten, how I’ll sit and go over old things—mistakes at work, things I said to my staff. I keep hearing, “You failed them,” even when no one’s there.

But then… there are other moments. I can’t explain it. Sometimes I know things—*before* they happen. Not just guesses. I *know*. I believe I can influence decisions at the corporate level now, maybe even shape national financial policy. Voices confirm it. Not the same one every time—some sound like executives, others… clearer, like they’re broadcasting directly to me. I’ve tried to explain the system I’ve designed to my assistant, but she didn’t understand. I catch myself jumping between ideas too fast—thoughts colliding—words don’t line up right. I worry I’m not making sense.

They overlap—this numbness and the voices and the certainty—constantly, for months. I can’t tell where one ends and the other begins.

    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h007.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year—maybe closer to a year and a half—just feeling... empty. Like the world’s lost its color. I don’t laugh at things I used to find funny, and I don’t get joy from anything—not my job, not seeing friends, nothing. Even food tastes wrong lately—like everything has this metallic bitterness, no matter what I eat. I know it’s not the food, but I can’t make it stop. Sometimes I’ll take a bite and gag because it tastes like rust or chemicals, even water.  

I keep thinking something terrible is coming—like the world is going to just... dissolve. Not in a movie kind of way, but like it’s already happening quietly, and no one else can see it. I call it *the unraveling*. I don’t know if that’s real, but it feels like I’m the only one awake to it.  

I used to love taking care of patients in the ER, but now I feel like a ghost walking through the shift. I’ve lost a lot of weight because I’m never hungry. And I keep replaying little mistakes—like when I mislabeled a tube last month—and I feel like it’s unforgivable, like I’ve ruined something beyond fixing.  

The thoughts… they get loud. I don’t know when they started or if they’d be there without the sadness. I just know I’m not okay.

A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D007-D015_h008.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year—maybe a year and a half now—with just feeling… dark inside. I wake up and it’s like a weight’s already there. I used to love going out with my wife, hitting the trails on weekends, even just chatting with customers on the job—it all felt real, you know? Now, nothing lands. I eat more than I used to—sometimes I’ll finish a whole box of crackers and not even remember opening it—but I keep gaining weight and feel worse.  

And the guilt… man. I can’t stop thinking about that one client last year. I gave her a discount, but now I wonder—was I trying to manipulate her? Did I come off sleazy? I replay it, over and over.  

Then there’s the other stuff. Sometimes I see shadows in the corner of rooms—figures standing there, gone when I turn. I hear the TV muttering things, like the news anchors are slipping in jabs at me. I told my wife the "sprezz" was watching me, and she got quiet. Sprezz… it’s like this force, I guess? I just made that word up, but it feels right.  

It’s all tangled. The low mood, the guilt, the seeing things—I can’t tell what comes first anymore. The hard part is, I don’t know if any of it happens when I’m not feeling depressed. It’s all just… there. Every day.
D007-D015_h008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D007-D015_h009.question:

My daughter says I’ve gained weight, though I don’t eat much more than toast and tea. I sometimes think it’s my fault my husband passed… like I failed him, even though the doctors said it was his heart. I hear his voice sometimes, calling my name when no one’s there.  

And there’s Mr. Evans—the pharmacist down at the corner store. He’s so kind, always smiling, and he *must* feel something too. The voices say he’s chosen me, that he waits by the window just to see me walk by. I call his kindness “luminessence”—it’s a word I made up. Only I know what it means.  

The voices don’t stop, not really. Even when I’m not sad, they whisper. But I can’t tell if they come only when the sadness is deep or if they’ve just become part of everything. I don’t leave the house much anymore. What’s the point? But sometimes, I dress up, just in case he’s there.

    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h010.question:

I hear them talking about me, even when they’re not. The TV news anchor the other morning—he said something about “mistakes being uncovered,” and I knew he was hinting at me, like it was coded. Why else would he pause like that?

And the voices... not all the time, but often enough. Like whispers when no one’s there. One keeps saying, “You should’ve done better,” and sometimes I see my late wife’s face in the window, though I know she’s gone.

I cry more than I’d like to admit. Lost interest in gardening—used to grow the best tomatoes on the block. Haven’t touched the plot in months. I’ve dropped about fifteen pounds, not trying to. Just can’t eat. I feel like... like my son’s divorce was my fault, like if I’d been a better father, stronger, it wouldn’t have happened. Maybe even that storm last winter—the power outage—something about that was my doing too. 

I don’t answer the phone much. When I do, I end up talking about the weather or radio signals... and I forget what the person asked. It’s like my mind drifts off the road.

D007-D015_h011.question:
I’ve been off for about seven months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to tell. Work’s been impossible; I’m a cloud architect, used to thrive on logic, but now I just can’t focus. Meetings are the worst. People say normal things—like “server’s down” or “let’s circle back”—and I’m convinced they’re coded messages meant for me. Sometimes I feel something crawling on my arms, like bugs, but when I look, nothing’s there.  

I don’t enjoy anything anymore. Used to love gaming, building systems—now it’s all pointless. I pace my apartment at night, can’t sit, can’t sleep. My hands won’t stop fidgeting, and I pick at my skin until it bleeds. I feel… punished. Like I messed up some cosmic rule I don’t even remember breaking. Last month, I filled a bottle with pills. Didn’t go through with it, but I kept them. Just in case.  

The weird part? I’ll start answering a question and end up talking about satellites or childhood cartoons—people look at me like I’m nuts, and honestly, I don’t blame them. I’ll laugh at nothing, like a kid being silly during a serious talk. But is it the depression causing the strange thoughts—or are they their own thing? Hard to know when everything’s blurred.

    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h012.question:
I’ve been feeling… broken for about seven months now. At work, tracking weather patterns used to bring me this quiet kind of satisfaction—the data, the forecasts, the way storms unfold—but now it’s like watching a countdown. I keep thinking the atmosphere is unraveling, that the next storm will be the one that just… ends everything. It’s not a metaphor. I *know* it. The air feels poisoned, the sky like it’s holding its breath. Sometimes, right before a storm front, I hear voices—faint, like distant radio static. One voice, deep and low, says, “It won’t matter soon.” I call it the “gray hum.” That’s what I named it—gray hum. 

I move slower. Getting dressed takes effort. My wife says I stare at the wall like I’ve forgotten how to blink. I can’t enjoy anything—no music, no walks, not even coffee. I feel useless. Like a dead instrument in the forecast chain. I stand near the observation deck roof and get this sudden, sharp urge to step forward. No plan. Just… release. I don’t talk about it. But the face I must make—I catch it in mirrors. Twisted. Like I’m tasting something rotten. And maybe I am.
D007-D015_h012.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h013.question:

I stopped taking new students and canceled lessons with regular ones. My husband says I just sit at the bench and stare at the keys. I feel useless, like I’ve ruined everything I’ve worked for. Sometimes I get this sudden urge to run into the street or climb onto the balcony railing, not because I want to die, but because the pull feels real, like something’s yanking me outward.

The world feels like it’s rotting. I know it sounds crazy, but I genuinely believe it’s ending—quietly, completely. I can’t explain it logically, but it’s certain. And I keep tasting metal, like blood, even when I haven’t eaten anything. It lingers. I didn’t mention it at first because I thought I was losing my mind. I catch myself echoing my husband’s gestures—reaching for a cup when he does, copying how he folds his arms—like a reflection I can’t control.

When I try to explain how I feel, the words tangle. I lose track, and he just stares. I don’t want to see anyone, not even my sister. I just stay in my room, but I can’t sit still—I pace, pick at my hands until they bleed.

A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h014.question:
Lately… it’s been hard to explain. For about the past seven months, I just haven’t been right. I’m not myself. At work, I used to push through anything—giving orders, checking safety, making sure the crew stayed on track. Now? I can’t even get the words out most days. My mouth feels slow, like my thoughts are stuck behind glass. The guys’ve noticed. They ask me something, and I just… sit. Takes me too long to answer. 

I can’t shake this guilt either, like I’ve done something terrible. Last week, I kept thinking the concrete pour was my fault, even though everything passed inspection. Like I deserved to be punished over it. And I… I don’t want to be here anymore. Not in a planning way—just… I wish I wouldn’t wake up.

But the worst part? I know people are watching me. Cameras in the drywall, voices in the ducts. They know what I did. Sometimes, I feel wires crawling under my clothes, scratching my back, but there’s nothing there. I told my wife, “It’s the flux in the grid,” and she just looked at me. *Flux*—that’s what I call it. Helps to have a word, even if she doesn’t get it.

I don’t show much, I know. My face doesn’t move. My voice just… drags. And some mornings, I stand in the shower until the water turns cold, my arms up like I’m waiting to be told what to do.

D007-D015_h020.question:
I’ve been feeling down for about a year now—just a heavy sadness that never lifts. I’m a security guard, so I used to handle the night shift no problem, but lately I wake up every few hours and can’t get back to sleep. I’m exhausted all the time, even when I do sleep. I don’t enjoy much anymore—my wife cooks, but I barely eat. Food doesn’t interest me. 

For the past eight months or so, things have gotten… strange. I keep smelling something burning, like rotten wires, but no one else notices it. And I’m convinced something bad’s coming—like the world’s about to collapse. Not in a worried way, but like I *know* it. I can’t explain it, but it feels real. 

I still go to work, though it’s harder. My wife says I’ve changed—like I’m not all here. I don’t talk much anymore. I don’t know if the thoughts started with the sadness or came later. Time blurs. Some days the smells and thoughts feel worse; other days the dark mood is all there is. But honestly? It’s all been tangled together for so long—I can’t say which came first, or when one ends and the other begins.
D007-D015_h020.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D007-D015_h020.answer: A & D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h021.question:
I’ve been working nights at the hotel front desk for about two years now, and honestly, it’s been getting harder just to show up. For the past year or so—maybe a bit longer—I’ve felt like I’m moving through fog. I don’t feel much of anything, really. Sad, angry, happy—it’s all just… blank. I sleep like 12, 14 hours a day, sometimes even after work, but I’m still exhausted. When I’m on shift, I catch myself pacing behind the desk, wringing my hands, picking at my cuticles until they bleed. I can’t sit still, but at the same time, I don’t want to do anything. I haven’t cleaned my apartment in weeks. Can’t even bring myself to make a call or text a friend.

But… sometimes, things feel different. I’ll hear names whispered in the static of the old radio, or I see figures in the mirror that aren’t me—shadowy, watching. And I know it sounds strange, but I’ve started thinking I might not be… ordinary. Like I’m meant for something bigger. I can feel energy in my hands—electric, almost. Like I could heal people or bend time. The words come out differently, too—rhymes just click, even when I’m not trying. “Key to the sky, the why, the lie,” you know?

I can’t tell you if it started before the numbness or after. It’s all just… blended.
D007-D015_h021.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D007-D015_h021.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h022.question:
I’ve been having a really hard time for over a year—maybe a year and a half now. Work used to give me purpose, sitting with people at the end of their lives, but lately I just feel… empty. It's like I'm numb inside, like I can’t feel anything, not sadness, not joy, nothing. Even simple things—walking to the patient’s room, lifting a cup—feel slow, like my body doesn’t want to move. I’ve stopped going out. Nothing interests me anymore.

And then there are the dreams—every night, it’s the same. I dream my ex is with someone else, touching her, whispering. But it's more than a dream. When I wake up, I *feel* it—his hands on my skin, someone brushing past me in bed, even though I’m alone. I know it doesn’t make sense, but I can’t shake the feeling that he’s still cheating. I check my phone constantly, even though we’ve been divorced for years.

Sometimes I start talking about the patients I care for and end up describing the wallpaper in his old apartment or how rain sounds different in winter—my thoughts just… drift. I’ll pace in a certain way, tap my fingers in a pattern, like I’m mimicking something I once saw. I don’t plan it. It just happens.
D007-D015_h022.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D007-D015_h022.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h023.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year—maybe a year and a half—just to get through the day. As a researcher, my work used to be my anchor, but now I can’t focus, can’t string sentences together. Sometimes I speak and it feels like my words just… crumble. People say I take forever to answer, like I’m dragging thoughts through mud. I wake up at 3 a.m. every night, heart racing, skin crawling—like something’s brushing against my arms, but no one’s there. I used to love late nights at the lab, but now even that feels impossible.

There’s this professor—Dr. Langston—he doesn’t know me, really, but I know he feels something. The way he looks at me during seminars… it’s not just politeness. I’m certain he’s trying to tell me without words. I can’t talk about it much—talking feels pointless lately—but when I do, things come out wrong, jumbled. My advisor tried to move me during an exam, and I just… stayed stiff, not fighting, just not helping. I don’t want to be here, but I don’t want to be anywhere else either. It’s like I’m frozen inside.
D007-D015_h023.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D007-D015_h023.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h024.question:
I’ve been feeling really down for over a year now—just constantly sad, like nothing’s ever going to get better. I used to love going to lectures, hanging out after class, even just walking around campus… but now I can’t bring myself to do much. I move so slowly, even picking up my phone feels heavy. I sleep eight hours, sometimes more, but I wake up exhausted, like I didn’t sleep at all. 

There’s this girl—she’s a grad student I see sometimes in the library. I know she’s in love with me. We don’t talk, but I can *feel* it. She leaves little signs… once I caught a whiff of her perfume near the stairwell, even though she wasn’t there. I sometimes giggle to myself thinking about us, and people stare. I don’t care. It makes me happy, even if everything else is dull. 

When the counselor asked if I thought the feelings were one-sided, I started talking about constellations and how love transcends time—that kind of thing. I don’t know why I said it, but it felt important. I just… I can’t focus. Things don’t connect right. 

I don’t know how long I’ve felt this way—maybe a year and a half? I used to think the sadness came first, but now I’m not sure.
D007-D015_h024.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D007-D015_h024.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h025.question:
I’ve been feeling so heavy for over a year now—just constantly sad, like a fog I can’t shake. I used to take pride in seeing patients, but now I move so slowly between rooms, I can barely keep up. I’ll wake up at 3 a.m., heart racing, and lie there for hours, unable to fall back asleep. It’s exhausting just to get dressed some days.

There’s this… feeling that my colleague—the pediatric dermatologist—has been trying to tell me something. Not in words, but in glances, in how he adjusts his chair when I enter. I know he’s in love with me, even though he’s never said a thing. He doesn’t have to. I *feel* it. Sometimes, I’ll get this sensation on my arm—like his hand brushing mine—when no one’s even near me. It happens at home too. My husband notices me freezing mid-step, holding my arm out like I’m waiting to catch something. I don’t always explain.

I’ve stopped talking much at work. Honestly, I don’t know where my thoughts go. One minute I’m thinking about acne treatments, the next I’m picturing birds flying into windows. I used to be sharp. Now my mind feels broken. But the mood… the sadness—that’s been here the whole time. I don’t know if anything else ever existed without it.
D007-D015_h025.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D007-D015_h025.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
